claims.text: Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical lamellar dual-phase microstructure comprising fcc and B2/bcc-type phases.
The untreated alloy has high strength under quasi-static loading.
The untreated alloy exhibits limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle failure.
Brittleness in the untreated alloy is caused by dislocation pile-ups at fcc/B2 or equivalent phase interfaces.
A low-temperature aging or annealing heat treatment can induce fine, coherent L12 precipitates in Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The heat treatment will locate the L12 precipitates preferentially along internal lamellar or interphase boundaries.
The boundary-associated L12 precipitates will be uniformly distributed.
Fine L12 precipitates strengthen the alloy through Orowan dislocation bowing and bypass.
The precipitates provide distributed barriers that break up large dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
Dislocation bypass around the precipitates will make plastic deformation more homogeneous.
Breaking up dislocation pile-ups will reduce local stress concentrations and mitigate microcracking.
Controlled L12 precipitation will contribute to work hardening.
The heat-treated alloy will retain or modestly increase yield strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile elongation than the untreated alloy.
Reduced boundary stress concentrations will delay crack initiation and catastrophic tensile failure.
The proposed benefits apply during room-temperature quasi-static tensile loading at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The treatment's effects may differ at high strain rates or elevated temperatures because other deformation mechanisms may dominate.
